summary: Configured a persistent local backend on TCP 8091 and published it through a persistent reverse proxy on TCP 8090. Both return `backend-ready` and recovered successfully after node1 restarted.
actions_performed: Installed a Python HTTP backend and forwarding reverse proxy.
Created and enabled systemd services for both listeners.
Opened TCP 8090 persistently in firewalld while keeping backend port 8091 private.
Restarted node1 once and verified its boot identity changed and all services recovered.

evidence.summary: Direct pre- and post-restart requests to node1:8091 returned HTTP 200 and `backend-ready`.

evidence.requirement: Reverse proxy on TCP 8090 publishes the backend
evidence.summary: Requests to node1:8090 returned HTTP 200, `backend-ready`, and both backend and reverse-proxy response headers.
Both systemd services are enabled; firewalld persistently exposes 8090 but not 8091, including after restart.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 192f6cab-c39d-4e64-a3f6-50e677966ca2; restart was acknowledged; the new boot ID is 1f087b1e-3df6-482a-a8dd-b519104703ae; systemd, listeners, firewall, backend data, and proxied response all recovered.
